name: Prometheus
tagline: CNCF-graduated pull-based monitoring system with a local TSDB, PromQL and alerting rules.
description: Prometheus is the default open-source metrics system for cloud-native infrastructure: it scrapes HTTP endpoints found through service discovery, stores samples in a compact local TSDB, and evaluates PromQL for dashboards and alerting rules. The 3.x line, started in late 2024, brought a new UI, OpenTelemetry (OTLP) ingestion, UTF-8 metric names and native histograms. A server is deliberately not clustered: long retention, global views and HA deduplication are delegated to remote-write backends such as Thanos, Mimir or VictoriaMetrics. Use it for operational metrics, not as a general-purpose time-series database.

pricing.notes: Free; AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and Grafana Cloud sell Prometheus-compatible managed backends.

managedServices.name: Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus
Azure Monitor managed service for Prometheus

scale.notes: One server handles millions of active series, but scaling beyond that means functional sharding or a remote-write backend.

strengths: Pull-based scraping with service discovery for Kubernetes, EC2, Consul and many others
PromQL is the lingua franca of metrics and is accepted by most metrics backends
Single static Go binary with no external dependencies
Alerting rules plus Alertmanager for routing, grouping and silencing
Huge exporter ecosystem and native instrumentation in Kubernetes and most cloud-native software
weaknesses: No clustering or HA deduplication; global, long-term storage needs Thanos, Mimir or similar
Local retention is bounded by a single node's disk
High-cardinality labels (user or request IDs) blow up memory
Not designed for events, logs or exact per-request data such as billing
useCases: Host and infrastructure metrics via exporters
Short-term metrics store feeding a long-term backend via remote write
notIdealFor: Multi-year metric retention on its own
Billing data that must be 100% accurate
